title: Licensing & the Road Test
summary: Riders under 18 must complete the Massachusetts Rider Education Program (MREP) basic rider course to get a motorcycle license. The course takes about 15 hours: 5 in the classroom and 10 on the motorcycle.
By law a motorcycle has a seat or saddle and is built to run on no more than three wheels touching the ground.

Mopeds (motorized bicycles) are limited to 30 mph and 50 cc by design and may not be ridden faster than 25 mph, with fines of up to $100 for breaking the moped rules; motorized scooters may not be ridden faster than 20 mph or between sunset and sunrise.

A limited use vehicle (top speed over 30 but not over 40 mph, with a certificate of origin and a 17-character VIN) needs a Class M license or permit if it is a motorcycle and may not use any road with a speed limit above 40 mph or limited-access highways.

To get a motorcycle learner's permit you must be at least 16, fill out an application, show valid ID, pay the fee, and pass the knowledge test; if you have no Class D license, you must pass the Class D knowledge test as well.
Permit holders may ride only from sunrise to sunset and may never carry passengers.

At 16 and a half you can apply for a Class M license, as long as your license or right to operate has not been revoked; the permit converts to a license only after you pass the road test or complete the MREP course.

Junior operators (under 18) must hold the permit for at least six months with a clean record before the road test, complete driver's education and the MREP basic rider course, and may not drive between 12:30 a.m. and 5:00 a.m.
Failing the motorcycle road test twice means you must complete an approved rider training course before scheduling another road test.

For the road test the motorcycle must be safe, registered, insured, and inspected (Massachusetts-registered motorcycles need a safety inspection every year), and the rider must wear a DOT helmet meeting FMVSS No. 218 plus eye protection unless the bike has a windshield or screen.
The manual says that if you take the road test on a trike or a limited use vehicle, your Class M license carries a 'J' restriction that limits you to that type of vehicle.
The road test may include figure-eights and 360-degree circles in both directions without putting a foot down, along with starts, stops, turns, traffic, intersections, and hills.

The manual's fee table lists $30 for a 2-year learner's permit, $35 for the license application and road test, $50 for a 5-year Class M license, and $15 to add a motorcycle endorsement to a license you already hold; fees can change.

questions.q: What is the minimum age to obtain a Massachusetts motorcycle learner's permit?
options: 16 and a half
questions.explanation: An applicant for a motorcycle learner's permit must be at least 16 years old.

questions.q: When is a motorcycle learner's permit holder allowed to ride?
options: Any time, if accompanied by a licensed rider
Only between 5:00 a.m. and 12:30 a.m.
Only during daylight hours, from sunrise to sunset
Any time, but only on roads posted 40 mph or less
questions.explanation: Permit holders may operate a motorcycle only in daylight, from sunrise to sunset. The manual makes no exception for riding with a licensed rider.

questions.q: May a motorcycle learner's permit holder carry a passenger?
options: No, passengers are prohibited for permit holders
No, unless the passenger holds a Class M license
Yes, during daylight hours only
Yes, if the passenger is over 18
questions.explanation: Riders on a learner's permit are not allowed to carry any passengers, not even one who holds a motorcycle license.

questions.q: What happens if you fail the Class M road test twice?
options: You must wait at least one year before scheduling another road test
You must retake and pass the knowledge test before scheduling another road test
Your learner's permit is revoked and you must apply for a new one
You must complete an approved rider training course before scheduling another road test
questions.explanation: After two failed motorcycle road tests, the RMV requires completion of an approved rider training course before another road test can be booked.

questions.q: A 17-year-old wants a Massachusetts motorcycle license. Which rider training course must they complete?
options: The Massachusetts Rider Education Program experienced rider course
The Massachusetts Rider Education Program basic rider course
An advanced street-riding course at a private school
No course is required if they pass the road test
questions.explanation: Anyone under 18 is required to successfully complete the MREP basic rider course to get a motorcycle license. The experienced rider course teaches advanced techniques, but it is not the required one.

questions.q: How long must a minor hold a learner's permit before taking the road test for a Junior Operator's License?
options: 30 days
3 months
6 months
12 months
questions.explanation: Junior operators must have held the learner's permit for at least six months, with a clean record over that period, before the road test.

questions.q: Under the Junior Operator's License rules, a driver under 18 may not drive during which hours?
options: Midnight to 4:00 a.m.
questions.explanation: The manual's Junior Operator's License rules bar drivers under 18 from driving between 12:30 a.m. and 5:00 a.m. A motorcycle learner's permit is stricter still: permit holders of any age may ride only from sunrise to sunset.

questions.q: Under Massachusetts law, a motorcycle is designed to travel on how many wheels in contact with the ground?
options: Exactly two
No more than four
Exactly three
No more than three
questions.explanation: The legal definition covers motor vehicles with a seat or saddle built to run on no more than three wheels touching the ground, so it includes both two-wheeled bikes and three-wheeled trikes.

questions.q: What is the maximum speed at which you may operate a moped (motorized bicycle) in Massachusetts?
options: 20 mph
25 mph
30 mph
40 mph
questions.explanation: Moped riders must not ride faster than 25 mph, whatever the moped itself can do.

questions.q: Which rule applies to operating a motorized scooter in Massachusetts?
options: It may be ridden on limited-access highways in the right lane
It may carry one passenger with a helmet
It may not be ridden faster than 20 mph
It must be registered with the RMV
questions.explanation: Motorized scooters are capped at 20 mph. The manual also says they cannot carry passengers, use limited-access highways, or be registered by the RMV.

questions.q: On which roads is a limited use vehicle prohibited?
options: Any road with a speed limit above 40 mph
Any road with a speed limit above 30 mph
Any road with more than two travel lanes
Any road after sunset
questions.explanation: Limited use vehicles may not be driven on limited-access or express highways or on any road posted above 40 mph.

questions.q: When is a motorcycle operator NOT required to wear eyeglasses, goggles, or a face shield?
options: When riding below 30 mph on local roads
When riding in daylight and clear weather
When wearing a DOT-approved helmet
When the motorcycle has a windshield or screen
questions.explanation: Eye protection is required unless the motorcycle is equipped with a windshield or screen. As safety advice, though, the manual says a windshield cannot take the place of a faceshield or goggles (page 14).

questions.q: During the Class M road test, how must you perform figure-eights and 360-degree circles?
options: In both directions, without your feet touching the roadway
In one direction only, with one foot down allowed
In one direction only, without your feet touching the roadway
In both directions, with a foot down allowed in tight turns
questions.explanation: The examiner may ask for figure-eights and full circles in both directions, completed without putting your feet down.

questions.q: To avoid being charged the road test fee, at least how far in advance must you cancel or reschedule your road test?
options: 24 hours
48 hours
72 hours
One week
questions.explanation: Cancelling or rescheduling less than 72 hours before the test time results in the road test fee being charged.

questions.q: How can you tell that a motorcycle helmet meets the federal safety standard Massachusetts requires?
options: It comes with an attached face shield
It carries stickers inside and outside
It is a bright color for visibility
It weighs at least three pounds
questions.explanation: Helmets that meet the federal standard required by state law are labeled with stickers on both the inside and the outside. A face shield, a bright color or a helmet's weight doesn't show that it meets the standard.

questions.q: About how long is the MREP basic rider course, according to the manual?
options: About 8 hours: 3 in the classroom and 5 on the motorcycle
About 15 hours: 5 in the classroom and 10 on the motorcycle
About 20 hours: 10 in the classroom and 10 on the motorcycle
About 15 hours, all of it spent on the motorcycle
questions.explanation: The manual describes the basic rider course as roughly 15 hours: 5 hours of classroom teaching and 10 hours of riding. To graduate you must attend every session and pass both a written test and a riding skills evaluation.

questions.q: By law, which limits must a moped (motorized bicycle) meet in Massachusetts?
options: A top speed of 40 mph or less and an engine of 100 cc or less
A top speed of 25 mph or less and an engine of 150 cc or less
A top speed of 30 mph or less and an engine of 50 cc or less
A top speed of 45 mph or less and an engine of 50 cc or less
questions.explanation: A moped is built to go no faster than 30 mph, has an engine of no more than 50 cubic centimeters, and has an automatic transmission.

questions.q: According to the manual, what is the most you can be fined for breaking one of the moped riding rules?
questions.explanation: Breaking any of the moped riding rules, such as using an off-street recreational path or skipping the helmet, can bring a fine of up to $100.

questions.q: How fast can a limited use vehicle go, by definition?
options: No faster than 25 mph
Faster than 30 mph but no faster than 40 mph
Faster than 40 mph but no faster than 55 mph
No faster than 20 mph
questions.explanation: By definition, a limited use vehicle has a top speed above 30 mph but not above 40 mph. Whether it is treated as a motorcycle or a passenger vehicle comes down to its number of wheels.

questions.q: Which of these is required for a limited use vehicle?
options: An engine of 50 cc or less
An 11-character VIN
A 17-character VIN
Pedals as well as a motor
questions.explanation: A limited use vehicle needs a 17-character vehicle identification number (VIN), a certificate of origin, and a manufacturer's statement that it satisfies the federal safety standards for its class. The manual sets no engine-size limit for a limited use vehicle.

questions.q: A permit holder wants to apply for a Class M license. What is the youngest age at which they may apply?
options: 16 years
17 years
16½ years
18 years
questions.explanation: You must be at least 16½ to apply for the Class M license, and your license or right to operate must not have been revoked. Applicants under 18 also fall under the junior operator rules.

questions.q: According to the manual's fee table, how much does a Class M learner's permit application cost, and how long is the permit good for?
options: $15, for 1 year
$25, for 3 years
$35, for 6 months
$30, for 2 years
questions.explanation: The manual lists $30 for a permit application, which covers a 2-year permit for Class B, C, D or M. The manual notes that all fees can change.

questions.q: You already hold a Class D license. According to the manual's fee table, what does it cost to add a motorcycle endorsement to it?
questions.explanation: The manual's fee table lists $15 to add a motorcycle endorsement to a license you already hold.

questions.q: How often must a motorcycle registered in Massachusetts pass a safety inspection?
options: Every two years
Once a year
Only when it is first registered
Every six months
questions.explanation: Motorcycles registered in Massachusetts need a safety inspection every year. For the road test you must show the examiner the registration and a valid inspection sticker.

questions.q: What does the manual list as the fee for a Class M license, and for how many years is the license valid?
options: $30, for 2 years
$35, for 3 years
$50, for 5 years
$75, for 10 years
questions.explanation: The manual's fee table lists $50 for a Class M license, which is good for 5 years.

questions.q: In the manual's fee table, what is the combined license application and road test fee?
questions.explanation: The manual lists a $35 license application and road test fee, the same for every license class.

questions.q: You don't have a Class D (car) license. What must you pass to get a motorcycle learner's permit?
options: Only the Class M knowledge test
The Class M knowledge test and a road test
Both the Class D and the Class M knowledge tests
A road test in place of any knowledge test
questions.explanation: If you don't hold a Class D license, the manual says you must pass both a Class D and a Class M knowledge test.
